newsitem.title: USA: US Senator asks Fed to adopt debit card policy.
newsitem.headline: US Senator asks Fed to adopt debit card policy.

text.p: Senator Jack Reed asked the Federal Reserve in a letter released Friday to adopt regulations alerting consumers of the potential risks of using debit cards.

"The Federal Reserve has a responsibility to ensure that regulations governing debit cards provide adequate consumer disclosures about the unique features of debit cards, including the risks for fraud and abuse," the Rhode Island Democrat said in a letter to Fed chairman Alan Greenspan dated Aug 12.

Debit cards often resemble credit cards or automated teller machine cards but are not covered by the same statutes that limit consumer liability in the event of theft or fraud. In the last few weeks, however, major debit card issuers have voluntarily agreed to limit consumer liability for unathorized use of a debit card to $50 or less.
Reed also said he intended to pursue debit card legislation protecting consumers when Congress came back into session in September.
